**What I did**

1. I checked the file. It holds 1233 rows, one per patient, and 19 columns. The analysed columns have no missing values. The harness data check referred to the column summary table, not to the patient data.
2. I ran a chi-square test for age group, sex and poverty. I ran a Fisher exact test for marital status, because one expected count was below 5 (smallest expected count 3.71).
3. I corrected the four univariate p-values with the Holm method.
4. I fitted a multivariable logistic regression of default (1 = defaulted, 0 = all other outcomes) on the six covariates. The unit of replication is one patient. n = 1233 patients, with 127 defaults (10.3 percent).

**Univariate tests (alpha = 0.05, two-sided, n = 1233 patients each)**

| Variable | Test | Statistic | Raw p | Holm-adjusted p |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Age group (4 levels) | Pearson chi-square, 3 df | chi-square 12.43 | 0.006 | 0.018 |
| Sex | Pearson chi-square, 1 df, no Yates correction | chi-square 16.90 | 0.00004 | 0.00016 |
| Marital status (4 levels) | Fisher exact | — | 0.742 | 0.742 |
| Poverty | Pearson chi-square, 1 df, no Yates correction | chi-square 4.48 | 0.034 | 0.069 |

- The four tests form one family. The Holm correction used four tests.
- After correction, age group and sex are significant at alpha 0.05. Marital status and poverty are not.
- Effect sizes (Cramér's V): age group 0.100, sex 0.117, marital status 0.035 (chi-square statistic, not used), poverty 0.060.

**Multivariable logistic regression (Wald 95% confidence intervals)**

Reference levels: drug use No, BMI Normal, MDR treatment No, weekly alcohol No, HIV status Negative, secondary education Yes.

| Covariate (level compared with reference) | Adjusted OR | 95% CI | p |

- Likelihood-ratio test of BMI (2 df): chi-square 7.27, p = 0.026.
- Likelihood-ratio test of HIV status (2 df): chi-square 14.06, p = 0.0009.
